title: Renewal conversation maps and technical advocacy
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a practical, conversation-driven playbook and QBR companion for CS managers and technical advocates to drive expansion conversations: Dedicated upgrades, Private deployments, and premium SLA add-ons. It is intentionally lightweight — use as a QBR slide supplement, pre-meeting prep, and a post-meeting action tracker.

Audience:
- CSMs and Technical Customer Engineers (TCEs)
- Customer exec sponsors and platform engineering stakeholders
- RevOps for tracking closed/won and forecast adjustments

High-level approach (one-liner):
Map the customer’s operational pain -> surface measurable impact -> propose a low-friction pilot path (canary/dedicated/priv) -> secure a technical PoC commitment + executive sponsor.

Conversation map (flow for a 30–45m QBR or renewal call):
1) Warm re-cap (3–5m): recent wins, top metrics (latency, error rate, monthly tokens).
2) Operational reality check (8–10m): current capacity, contention events, incidents, cost surprises. Use specific examples (dates, routes, token volumes).
3) Business impact (8–10m): translate failures/limits to lost product features, user friction, revenue risk. Bring a simple cost-of-failure estimate.
4) Solution framing (8–10m): Dedicated / Private / SLA tiers mapped to their problems. Highlight tradeoffs (capex vs opex, time-to-migrate, controls).
5) Next steps + commitments (4–7m): technical pilot owners, timeline, decision criteria, exec sponsor.

QBR slide checklist (short bullets to use inside QBR):
- Title slide: QBR date, CSM, TCE
- One-pager metrics snapshot: 30/90/365 token volume, 95th latency, P99 latency, error rate
- Recent incidents and mitigations (timeline with impact)
- Cost summary (hosted spend vs estimated Dedicated break-even)
- Opportunity map: features currently blocked by capacity/security
- Proposed path (Pilot -> Validation -> Rollout) with success criteria
- Ask: decision owner, budget window, timeline

Technical pre-qualifier (to run before the QBR if possible):
- Current model(s) in use (name, version, sequence length distribution)
- Peak and sustained RPS and tokens per minute
- Percent of requests that require low latency (<250ms)
- Data residency/compliance constraints (yes/no)
- Any on-prem constraints (air-gapped? custom KMS?)
- Integration surface: SDKs, VPC peering, network egress allowance

Risk signals that trigger an upsell conversation:
- Repeated P99 breaches or escalations in last 90 days
- Monthly spend trending +30% QoQ without corresponding throughput increase
- Feature backlog items blocked by rate limits or security needs
- Customer request for stricter SLAs, audit logs, or private deployment

Proposed play: Dedicated upgrade (short pilot):
- Goal: demonstrate predictable latency under peak, prove cost-per-1000-token
- Duration: 4–6 weeks (pilot: 2 weeks smoke + 2–4 weeks load validation)
- Deliverables: dedicated GPU pool config, baseline latency/cost dashboard, failure-mode runbook
- Success criteria (pick 2–3): sustained target P95 latency, <5% error rate, cost delta within agreed threshold
- Typical blockers: network setup, billing commit, custom model compatibility

Proposed play: Private deployment (for regulated customers):
- Goal: full control over data plane, KMS integration, SOC/ISO evidence
- Duration: 8–12 weeks (varies with infra & security reviews)
- Deliverables: VPC design doc, compliance checklist, migration runbook, rollback plan
- Success criteria: pass internal security checklist, demo end-to-end with sample traffic, timeline for cutover agreed
- Typical blockers: procurement lead times, internal security review cycles, air-gap constraints

Proposed play: Premium SLA add-on (fastest path to risk reduction):
- Goal: guaranteed uptime/latency, priority incident handling, longer retention for observability
- Duration: 1–2 weeks to attach SLA to account (contract + config)
- Deliverables: SLA schedule, escalation contacts, extended logging & retention enabled
- Success criteria: customer signs SLA amendment and observes faster incident response times in next 90 days

Outreach templates (use plain, short versions in Slack/email):
- Pre-QBR Prod Nudge (to TSE or infra contact): "Quick ask before our QBR: can you send the last 3 incident timestamps and whether they were capacity or model related? This helps tailor the Dedicated/Private proposal."
- Executive hook (email): "We’ve identified 3 production edge cases where Dedicated capacity or a premium SLA would materially reduce risk and enable feature X. Can we align a 15-min exec chat to review?"

Renewal tracker (ASCII mini-table — keep this copy/paste-friendly):
- Customer | Renewal date | Current tier | Upsell target | Pilot owner | Status | Next action
- AcmeCorp | 2026-06-15 | Hosted Standard | Dedicated 2k GPUs | Samir Khan | at_risk | schedule-network-call
- BrightApps | 2026-04-04 | Hosted Plus | Private trial | Ethan Li | discovery | security-questions-sent

Triage decision quick guide (one-line each):
- If >2 incidents in 90d and revenue at risk -> propose premium SLA immediately.
- If latency variability + cost concerns -> propose Dedicated pilot.
- If compliance or data residency request -> propose Private evaluation.

Measurement and handoff artifacts (what TCE/SE should deliver):
- Pilot runbook with baseline and target metrics
- Cost model spreadsheet (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with assumptions
- Migration checklist (network, auth, model versions, rollback)
- Executive summary one-pager for procurement

Open questions / TODOs (items to refine in next revision):
- Create templated cost model sheet per common usage profiles (chat-heavy, embedding-heavy). TODO: ask FinOps for typical margins.
- Add a short script for the 10-minute exec decision call.
- Confirm SLA attachment lead time for EMEA customers (legal/local regs).

Quick wins and hacks (short):
- Offer a 2-week Dedicated smoke test for free credits to remove procurement friction.
- Pre-fill a security questionnaire template for Private prospects to accelerate SecOps review.
- Bundle extended logs + 24/7 pager for first 90 days after migration to surface early wins.

Files to attach to final playbook (placeholders):
- linked_artifacts:CONFLUENCE-1234 (pilot templates)
- JIRA-RND-987 (pricing calc epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proposals/pull/42 (proposal draft)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short and editable; drop into QBR slide deck as a single appendix slide.
- Lean on TCEs for pre-QBR technical pre-qualifier — most customers will not have answers without prompting.
- Track pilot outcomes in CRM with clear tags (dedicated_trial, private_eval, sla_addon).
